- If sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >1.0) in recent days, reduce forecast overshoots; model tends to overreact.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -1.0), avoid downward revisions; model often undercorrects.
- When model shows a sharp upward spike followed by a steep decline, reduce the magnitude of the spike in forecast.
- If forecast mean is consistently higher than true outcome over 3–5 days, apply a downward bias correction (e.g., subtract 0.5–1.5% of forecast value).
- If sentiment history shows repeated volatility (e.g., alternating +/– spikes), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecasts with 3–5 day moving average.
- For horizon >14 days, model tends to overestimate mean reversion; adjust by reducing final forecast by 0.3–0.8% per day beyond 14 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.5), model often misjudges trend direction; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 5-day mean.
